sections.heading: Idioms understood everywhere
sections.body: These idioms are understood across the Spanish-speaking world:

head: Idiom
Literally
Meaning
rows: to cost an eye of the face
to cost an arm and a leg
to put your foot in it
to have no hairs on the tongue
to be a piece of cake
to hit the nail on the head
to be up to the crown of the head

sections.heading: Regional favourites
sections.body: Some colourful regional ones: *¡Qué padre!* (Mexico — how cool!), *¡Qué chévere!* (Caribbean, Colombia, Venezuela — great!), *¡Qué bacán!* (Chile, Peru — cool!), *estar pato* (Chile — to be broke), *ser buena onda* (Mexico, and widely — to be a nice person), *echar la mala onda* (to spoil the mood). Use the neutral ones until you know where you are.

Mi abuela no tiene pelos en la lengua.
My grandmother speaks her mind.
El examen fue pan comido.
The exam was a piece of cake.
Está lloviendo a cántaros.
It's pouring down.
¡Diste en el clavo!
You hit the nail on the head!
¿Me echas una mano con la mudanza?
Can you give me a hand with the move?
Estoy hasta la coronilla de este ruido.
I'm fed up with this noise.
Si quieres aprobar, ponte las pilas.
If you want to pass, get your act together.
Las cosas van de mal en peor.
Things are going from bad to worse.
Tu novio es muy buena onda.
Your boyfriend is really nice.
¡Qué padre tu casa!
Your house is so cool!
¡Qué chévere la fiesta!
The party is great!
